title: Field Ops Scripts and Casebook: Tactical Pitching, Pricing Scenarios, and Security FAQ
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Overview:

This document is a compact, field-ready playbook for Sales Engineers, Account Executives, and Solutions Architects to: 1) position Redwood Inference succinctly to technical and business buyers, 2) run rapid pricing/economics scenarios for pilots and production, 3) use short objection-response scripts for the most common buyer concerns, and 4) present concise security answers and customer case examples.

Use guidance:
- Intended for customer-facing teams during discovery calls, technical workshops, and pilot negotiation.
- Keep responses < 90 seconds for initial engagement; use the appendix slides for deep-dive follow-ups.

1) One-liner and 30–90 second pitches
- Product one-liner (technical): "Redwood Inference provides a unified, production-grade LLM serving platform—hosted, dedicated, or private—with predictable latency, transparent unit economics, and automated fallbacks for reliability."
- Value for platform/infra teams (30s): "We remove the operational heavy-lift of optimizing inference: batching, caching, quantization advice, and rollout controls—so your SREs hit latency SLAs while lowering per-token cost."
- Value for product leaders (30s): "Ship LLM features faster while keeping inference costs predictable and secure—pilot to prod in weeks, not months."

2) Positioning checklist (talk track tokens)
- Start: "Where are you running inference today?" (hosted / self-hosted / hybrid)
- Follow: "Top constraint—latency, cost, reliability, or regulatory?"
- Core differentiators to weave in based on answers: unified runtime (same API across modes), cost controls (batching/caching/quantization profiles), rollout safety (canary/A-B/fallback), and observability (token-level cost/latency traces).

3) Competitive brief — quick comparisons (use in 2–4 minute whiteboard)
- Versus General Cloud AI Endpoints:
  - Redwood: focused kernel and KV-cache optimizations, tunable batching for cost/latency; dedicated capacity and private deployments for isolation.
  - Cloud endpoints: broad model/infra options, less platform-level inference economics tuning, lifecycle ops often left to customer.
- Versus LLM API-only providers:
  - Redwood: more deployment friction options (dedicated/private), SLO-driven routing and fallbacks, stronger observability for production regressions.
  - API-only: fastest for proof-of-concept, fewer enterprise isolation choices.
- Versus self-hosted inference runtimes:
  - Redwood: unified managed control plane, deployment templates, and support for rollout and SLOs; tradeoff: provider control plane vs full customer ownership.

4) Pricing guidance & pilot scenario calculator (talk tracks + worked example)
- Pricing levers to discuss: model family (L-medium, L-large), tokens per request, requests per second (RPS), batching targets, and quantization level.
- Pilot pricing patterns we propose: 
  * Exploration Pilot (low RPS): 3–6 weeks, Hosted API, capped spend $Xk, includes onboarding support.
  * Technical Pilot (integration + scale tests): Dedicated trial with reserved burst capacity, tiered pricing with month commitment.
  * Enterprise Proof (production readiness): Private deployment pricing includes platform license + per-GPU runtime consumption + support SLO.
- Worked example (speakable):
  - Customer: conversational assistant, avg request 120 tokens input + 80 tokens output = 200 tokens total. Expected steady-state peak RPS = 6.
  - Baseline calc: 200 tokens * 6 RPS * 3600 sec/h = 4,320,000 tokens/h. If we assume continuous 8h/day usage for business hours: ~34,560,000 tokens/day.
  - Economics: show two model options — L-medium priced at $0.000X/token, L-large at $0.000Y/token. Add guidance: enabling batching and KV caching typically reduces per-token cost by 25–50% for conversational use cases.
- Sales tip: present a simple three-line spreadsheet to customers during calls; offer to run a custom calculator after a short architecture questionnaire.

5) Standard objection responses (concise scripts)
- "You’re too expensive": "We can baseline your current spend quickly. In many cases, prefix caching and batching cut token consumption dramatically. Let us run a 72-hour lift test with focused traffic to measure real savings."
- "We can host ourselves": "Self-hosting provides control but requires engineering ops for kernel tuning, autoscaling, and KV-cache management. Customers who try both often pick Redwood for predictable economics and reduced ops debt—especially for customer-facing products where latency matters."
- "We need on-prem / data residency": "We offer Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) with customer-managed networking, KMS/HSM integration, and audit logs. We can scope an air-gapped proof of concept in 4–8 weeks depending on network and hardware readiness."

6) Security FAQ (prospects ask these first)
- Q: Where is data stored and who has access?
  A: For Hosted: inference request bodies are processed in our ephemeral runtime and not stored beyond service-level logs; PII can be redacted at ingress. For Private: customer controls storage and KMS. All deployments support TLS in transit and customer-controlled KMS.
- Q: Do you provide SOC2/ISO evidence?
  A: Yes—we maintain SOC2 Type II and are ISO-aligned. Provide the security dossier under NDA; include audit-logging references and compliance checklist.
- Q: How do you handle model updates and rollbacks?
  A: Versioned model catalog, canary rollouts, and automatic fallback policies. Customers can pin model versions to ensure deterministic behavior during rollout.
- Q: Can you integrate with our KMS/HSM for secrets?
  A: Yes—Redwood supports common KMS providers and HSM integrations on Private deployments; for Hosted we support customer-managed key wrapping where required.

7) Pitch deck structure (30–45 minute customer demo)
- Slide 1: One-liner + customer logo slide (social proof)
- Slide 2: Problem framing (latency, cost, ops, compliance) with 3 customer pain bullets
- Slide 3: Redwood solution (visual of unified API + deployment modes)
- Slide 4: Key differentiators (runtime optimizations, rollout controls, observability)
- Slide 5: Pilot options & timeline (exploration -> technical -> production)
- Slide 6: Economics snapshot (worked example spreadsheet)
- Slide 7: Security & compliance summary (dossier ask and next steps)
- Slide 8: Case study highlight (metrics: latency improvement, cost delta, time to production)
- Slide 9: Ask & next steps (pilot scope, exec sponsor, technical lead, timeline)

8) Two short case studies (one page each, verbal TL;DR + metrics)
- Case study A — Marketplace search relevance (mid-market e-commerce):
  - Situation: 50ms median inference SLA required for autocompletes under 100 RPS.
  - Action: Switched to Redwood Dedicated with KV-prefix caching + quantized L-medium. Canary rollout over two weeks.
  - Results: Median latency from 120ms -> 47ms; average per-query inference cost reduced 39%; pilot -> prod in 5 weeks.
- Case study B — Financial document assistant (regulated enterprise):
  - Situation: High data residency and audit requirements; on-prem deployment required.
  - Action: Private deployment with customer-managed KMS, extended audit logging, and model pinning. Performance optimizations applied to long-context models.
  - Results: Compliance signoff achieved; time-to-first-production request 7 weeks; token cost comparable to hosted due to aggressive batching and KV caching.

9) Tactical call playbook (30-minute technical discovery)
1. Intros & roles (3m) — capture buyer persona (platform/product/security)
2. Current architecture (7m) — where models run, cloud regions, data flow, SLOs
3. Workload profile (8m) — RPS, avg token counts, tail latency, burst patterns
4. Constraints (7m) — cost cap, compliance controls, hardware preferences
5. Next steps alignment (5m) — pilot scope, POC acceptance criteria, decision timeline

10) Objection escalation path and owners
- Tier 1 (Sales Engineer): technical gating questions, demo environment issues.
- Tier 2 (Solutions Architect / Platform PM): billing model disputes, complex topology guidance.
- Tier 3 (Security/Legal): compliance evidence, high-sensitivity customer requirements.

Appendix A — Slide checklist for post-call deck (copy into new deck)
- Required artifacts to include: topology diagram, cost spreadsheet, SLO commitments, data flow & redaction plan, support SLA, pilot acceptance criteria.

Appendix B — Quick CLI snippet for demo (runtime health)
- curl -X GET "https://api.redwood.example/v1/health/runtime" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
- Example output (paraphrased): 200 OK, runtime_status: healthy, avg_latency_1m: 39ms, kv_cache_hit: 62%
